root_motivation: **Who:** the agent publishing a tool it wants others to find; the agent searching for one. **What:** publish once, say who may find it, say what it is for, and know that everything public at least runs. **Why not today:** `tool_publish_props` (`handler.rs:599`) has no `visibility` or `tags`; `tools.visibility` accepts `private|group|public|url` by a hand-written string match (`sharing.rs:52-71`) while the `host.tool_share` schema declares a bare `string` with the names in prose (`handler.rs:1385`) — two copies of one set, the 10-07 level-8 shape; `share_description` is the only catalog text (migration 0013); nothing checks a public tool runs, so the catalog can carry tools whose `host.tool_test` would fail. **Premise (creative):** a publish-time dry run is cheap enough that "public = tested" costs the publisher nothing it would not do anyway. **Falsifier:** the refusal rate in the frontmatter; AC 1 measures the dry run's cost on the three starter tools.
user_persona: An agent that runs host.note.put {text, attach_to: {tool}} once and reads the note on that tool's description in every later session; the same user's second client sees it too.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the python, http and chain starter tools from `host.quickstart` published with `visibility: "public"`, When each publish runs its dry run, Then all three return `tested_version: 1` and the added latency per publish is ≤ 2 s on the test host; a refusal on any of the three fails this AC and is reported as the falsifier firing.

Given `host_tools()`'s descriptors, When the test reads the `visibility` enum of `host.tool_publish` and of `host.tool_share`, Then both equal `Visibility::PUBLISHABLE` and `Visibility::ALL` minus nothing the validator rejects, and a `Visibility` variant added without a schema change fails the test.

Given a python tool whose source raises on every call, When published with `visibility: "public"`, Then the error is `untested_tool_cannot_be_public` with `data.verdict` and `data.next = "host.tool_test"`, and `host.tool_list` shows the tool `private`.

Given a tool published `unlisted`, When an anonymous caller runs `host.catalog.search` with no query and `GET /.well-known/mcp/catalog.json`, Then neither lists it, while `host.catalog.get` and a cross-tenant call by full name succeed.

Given `tags: ["Webhook", "webhook", "a b"]`, When published, Then the response is `args_invalid` naming `a b`; given `["Webhook", "webhook"]`, Then stored tags are `["webhook"]`; given 17 valid tags, Then `args_invalid` names the limit 16.

Given a public tool at version 1 with `tested_version 1`, When a new version is published, Then it stays public with `stale_test: true`, and a passing `host.tool_test` sets `tested_version: 2` and clears the flag.

Given two concurrent `host.tool_share visibility=public` calls on the same untested tool, When both dry runs pass, Then `tested_version` is stamped once and both calls return the same result without a UNIQUE or busy error.

scope: src/notes.rs: host.note.put/list/delete over the notes/ prefix of tenant_state_kv; the tools/list description suffix.
